answer: Make rewards depend on unique measurements, not the number of reporters. A pearl farm buys one observation per buoy and time slot across its coastal horizon. A signed beacon supplies the slot ID; the ledger accepts one sensor-authenticated reading and marks that ID paid. Copying it through 1,000 agent keys yields one reward. To earn more, an attacker must collect genuinely additional requested measurements, paying for sensors and deployment. Bind signatures to location and time, and audit devices; self-issued sensor identities would reopen the loophole.
